chunk_map.heading: The best mitigation is the door you don't open

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 5 "Should the agent have write access to that system?" and "that mailbox". Harm (reader cannot tell what is pointed at) absent: the deictic is generic, bound to the reader's own candidate system, and "the agent" binds to "an agent" in line 3.
Closest: line 9 "this training included" names the training, not a file or position; no pointer to another file in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no "the X you did/saw/caught" backward reference in the body

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no demo, guess cue or reveal on the slide

rules_evaluated.evidence: line 3 "The cheapest, most reliable way to reduce risk on an agent is to not open the door in the first place." is a self-carrying claim; the slide has four paragraphs of content.
Header line 1 "The best mitigation is the door you don't open"; line 3 unpacks the metaphor ("not open the door") and lines 5-7 carry it through. Body does not contradict it.

Closest: line 5 three "Should the agent..." questions (anaphora triple); the third leg carries new content (customer-facing drafting, human drafts and agent reviews), so it passes. "cheapest, most reliable" (line 3) is a claim about the practice, not a self-grading superlative about the training. grep "Not X. Not Y." none; no number+retraction; "name, mitigate or re-test" (line 7) three concrete verbs.
